rows.question: 5 appearance unit
rows.answer: A goalie appearance of any length is a game played (7.6 seconds is the record low); goalie records count appearances, not starts. An emergency backup gets a game and a win.

rows.question: 7 early assists
rows.answer: The NHL itself says its 1917-1987 records needed 6,000+ fixes, and that in some years up to four assists were awarded on a goal.

receipts.quote: Six years of poring over scoresheets and summaries of games between 1917 and 1987 by an NHL statistics team has found and fixed more than 6,000 bits of information that were overlooked or miscounted in the league's early eras.
There were years when up to four assists were awarded on a goal.

rows.question: 7 early assists
rows.answer: Early assists were scarce and rules-dependent: offensive-zone only, secondary assists not full-time until 1945-46.

receipts.quote: Assists were also originally awarded only on passes within the offensive zone, and, after some on and off experimenting, secondary assists weren’t handed out full-time until the 1945-46 season onward.

rows.question: 8 ties/OTL/SO
rows.answer: NHL standings count only regulation defeats as losses, so an OT/SO run is a "winless streak"; ESPN pushes back and counts all defeats.

receipts.quote: because the NHL only considers it a loss when the defeat occurs in regulation
I know this is a real wacky concept, but a loss is a loss, and the Sabres have 18 of them in a row.

rows.question: 8 ties/OTL/SO
rows.answer: Streak definitions: undefeated = wins + ties; winless = regulation, OT, SO losses and ties; losing = regulation losses (plus OT losses 1983-99). Point totals are not comparable across 1983, 1999 and 2005.

receipts.quote: A winless streak includes losses in regulation, overtime, shootouts, or ties.

These changes in points awarded therefore make strict comparisons in wins, losses, and ties (after overtime, 1983–99, and in regulation, 1999–present) before and after these dates slightly problematic.

rows.publisher: Wikipedia (List of NHL statistical leaders / head coaches)
rows.question: 8 ties/OTL/SO
rows.answer: Points percentage = (2W + T + OTL) / 2GP; a 0-0 game decided by shootout gives both goalies a shutout; a shootout win counts as a goalie win (Brodeur's 48 included 10 SO wins).

receipts.quote: Points percentage is determined by the number of points a team earns (equal to the number of ties and overtime losses, plus twice the number of wins) divided by the total possible points (equal to twice the number of games).
Since 2005-06, if the game ends in a shootout after a 0-0 scoreless tie, both teams' goaltenders are credited with a shutout, regardless of how many shots are conceded during the shootout.
Most ties, career: Terry Sawchuk, 172
